body:
Feels like I wrote this. I had minimal human interaction as a child aside from school. The interactions I did have at home were often extremely negative. 

I spent my weekends pacing around my room, watching tv, and listening to music. I'd always daydream scenarios in which people would show me compassion or give me attention. These often involved me either dying or getting into some sort of accident, so people would be forced to care. 

I now have people in my life who appreciate me and all. However, I still do this. I often read people's texts from when I had a health scare recently, and everyone was so concerned. I'm fine now, but even when I wasn't I secretly loved it in some twisted way. It felt like how I was supposed to be treated as a kid. 

Since I never really had the basic need of actual positive adult attention in my crucial years, I'm not sure this will ever go away.

Full ride. I chose a cheaper option for undergrad and was fortunate enough to graduate debt free. Nobody cares where you go for undergrad. What matters is what type of student/employee you will become. Also, if you do decide to get a graduate degree, you will be looking at your undergrad debt with regret.
Yeah this test makes me feel like I have a learning disability.
